title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
author: Dick, Philip K.

highlights.text: That had been the ultimate incentive of emigration: the android servant as carrot, the radioactive fallout as stick. The U.N. had made it easy to emigrate, difficult if not impossible to stay. Loitering on Earth potentially meant finding oneself abruptly classed as biologically unacceptable, a menace to the pristine heredity of the race.
The silence of the world could not rein back its greed. Not any longer. Not when it had virtually won.
“In a magazine you come across a full-page color picture of a nude girl.” He paused. “Is this testing whether I’m an android,” Rachael asked tartly, “or whether I’m homosexual?”
“The distinct advantage of a goat is that it can be taught to butt anyone who tries to steal it.” “Not if they shoot it with a hypno-dart and descend by rope ladder from a hovering hovercar,”

“You will be required to do wrong no matter where you go. It is the basic condition of life, to be required to violate your own identity. At some time, every creature which lives must do so. It is the ultimate shadow, the defeat of creation; this is the curse at work, the curse that feeds on all life. Everywhere in the universe.”
Do androids dream? Rick asked himself. Evidently; that’s why they occasionally kill their employers and flee here. A better life, without servitude.

“Everything is true,” he said. “Everything anybody has ever thought.” He snapped on the car motor. “Will you be all right?” “I’ll be all right,” he said, and thought, And I’m going to die. Both those are true, too.
